findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Tighten AC5's verify command so it confirms the anchor link is located in the intro portion of the file (e.g., restrict the grep to the lines before the first `##` body section, or add a companion grep for the intro paragraph containing the anchor).
evidence: AC5 text: 'The intro anchor link resolves to the new section heading'

The grep matches any occurrence in the file, including the heading line itself if the anchor were rendered as text, or a link placed anywhere other than the intro — it does not confirm the link is in the intro
findings.finding: AC5's verify step does not confirm the anchor link appears in the *intro* specifically; it only confirms the anchor string `#preview-the-review-locally-before-you-push` exists somewhere in the file, yet AC5's text explicitly names it an 'intro anchor link'.
scenarios: An implementer could place the anchor link at the bottom of the file or inside the new section itself, satisfy the grep, yet not fulfil the stated 'intro cross-link' deliverable from the Scope.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the AC5 verify with a two-part check: first confirm the anchor string exists (current grep), then confirm the link appears before the first `## ` section heading other than a title — e.g., `awk '/^## /{found++} found==1 && /#preview-the-review-locally-before-you-push/{exit 0} END{exit 1}' src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile AC1 and AC5 to name the same heading: either update AC5's anchor to `#preview-the-review-locally` (matching the shorter heading in AC1 and Scope) or update AC1's heading string and the Scope description to `## Preview the review locally before you push`.
evidence: GitHub anchor generation: heading `## Preview the review locally` → anchor `#preview-the-review-locally`, NOT `#preview-the-review-locally-before-you-push`
findings.finding: AC1 asserts heading `## Preview the review locally` while AC5's anchor `#preview-the-review-locally-before-you-push` implies a longer heading `## Preview the review locally before you push`. An executor who creates the shorter heading (satisfying AC1 literally) will generate anchor `#preview-the-review-locally`, causing AC5's grep to fail; an executor who creates the longer heading may satisfy both but produces a heading name inconsistent with the Scope description.
scenarios: Executor creates `## Preview the review locally` per AC1 → AC5 grep finds no match → spurious AC5 failure even though intent is satisfied.
Executor creates longer heading to satisfy AC5 → AC1 still passes (substring match) but the heading text diverges from the Scope description and the rejected-duplicate concern.
findings.suggested_fix: Update AC5 to `grep -q '#preview-the-review-locally' src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` to match the heading `## Preview the review locally` asserted by AC1. The intro anchor link in scope should also reference `#preview-the-review-locally`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen AC5's proving command to verify the heading itself exists (e.g. `grep -q '^## Preview the review locally' src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md`) rather than checking for an occurrence of the anchor string, which can appear in the link rather than the heading.
evidence: Taxonomy item 4 (fixture invalidity): the grep matches the reference link, not the heading definition
AC1's `grep -q '## Preview the review locally'` checks for the heading, but (as noted above) names a different anchor than AC5
findings.finding: AC5's proving command (`grep -q '#preview-the-review-locally-before-you-push' ...`) checks only that the anchor string appears somewhere in the file, not that the heading generating that anchor actually exists. If an executor adds only the cross-link `[see here](#preview-the-review-locally-before-you-push)` without a matching heading, AC5 passes while the anchor remains broken.
scenarios: An agent satisfies AC5 by writing a link `[section](#preview-the-review-locally-before-you-push)` in an introduction without creating the corresponding heading — the anchor is dangling and the link silently 404s on GitHub.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace AC5's grep with: `grep -qE '^## Preview the review locally' src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` — this directly verifies the heading (and therefore the GitHub-generated anchor) exists, rather than checking for the anchor string which could appear in any cross-reference link.

evidence: verify command `grep -q 'REBAR_VERIFY_ENABLE_CODE_REVIEW' src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md && grep -q '## Preview the review locally' src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` greps the unanchored word 'REBAR_VERIFY_ENABLE_CODE_REVIEW' — it substring-matches (e.g. 'review_REBAR_VERIFY_ENABLE_CODE_REVIEW'); anchor it (\b, ^$, or a quoted key like '"REBAR_VERIFY_ENABLE_CODE_REVIEW":')

verify command `grep -q 'rebar review-code — optional local preview' src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` greps the unanchored word 'rebar' — it substring-matches (e.g. 'review_rebar'); anchor it (\b, ^$, or a quoted key like '"rebar":')

verify command `grep -q 'preview the review locally with .rebar review-code' AGENTS.md` greps the unanchored word 'preview' — it substring-matches (e.g. 'review_preview'); anchor it (\b, ^$, or a quoted key like '"preview":')
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.
